name: Mail service | Dockerised mailer
tagline: Outgoing mail for my applications: Postfix and OpenDKIM on Docker Swarm, reusing Traefik's TLS certificates.

keyPoints: A Postfix relay restricted to my domains, with SMTP authentication from a Docker secret.
TLS certificates extracted from Traefik's certificate store, with Postfix reloaded whenever they are renewed.
Reachable by applications through a dedicated overlay network.

popTagline: Set up so my applications can send verification and order emails without a third-party provider.

overview.mainContent: The mail service is a Docker Swarm stack of four services: Postfix, OpenDKIM, a certificate extractor and a reloader. Applications join its network and send mail through Postfix, which has it signed by OpenDKIM.
keyPoints: Certificates read from the file Traefik renews, watched for changes.
A small reloader image signalling Postfix when new certificates are in place.

purpose.title: Purpose
keyPoints: To send transactional emails (account verification, password reset, orders) from my own domain.
To understand what email deliverability requires: DKIM, TLS, DNS records.

constraints.title: Constraints
keyPoints: No additional certificate management: reuse what Traefik already renews.

choices.title: Reusing Traefik's certificates
choices.mainContent: Instead of a second certificate client, a container extracts the mail domain's certificate and key from Traefik's store, and writes them again whenever it changes.

choices.title: Signalling through a shared volume
choices.mainContent: The extractor drops a signal file in a shared volume. The reloader watches for it and asks Postfix to reload its configuration: a certificate renewal needs no restart.

challenges.title: Deliverability
challenges.mainContent: Self-hosted mail is easily flagged as spam: DKIM signing, correct DNS records and TLS were all needed before messages reached inboxes reliably.

keyPoints: Email is an old protocol, with many unwritten rules.
